claim_en: THE GATHERER FOUND. Scripture speaks in disparagement: the first Sabbath kept, the second desecrated. 'Gathering' is a LABOR, not a man's name — detaching from the ground (the Sifrei), collecting (Onkelos): the labor itself a recorded question. Who he was: Zelophehad by R. Akiva's verbal analogy on 'wilderness' (15:32 / 27:3) against R. Yehuda b. Beteira (one of the bold ones, 14:44) — unresolved, data on the entity. 'They found' — Moses appointed watchers.
middah: plain (the disparagement; the participle read as a labor, not a name — refuted from 15:33's repetition; the identity dispute recorded unresolved, R. Akiva's arm an I2/E7 verbal analogy on 'wilderness' 15:32 / 27:3; the watchers)

claim_en: THE WARNING SPECIFIES THE LABOR. 'Those who found him gathering' repeats 15:32 to teach that they WARNED him and he continued; R. Yitzchak: warning itself follows a-fortiori from idolatry (the gravest, not liable without it), so the repetition teaches that the warning must NAME THE LABOR — for every primary labor of the Torah. 'To Moses and to Aaron': invert the verse (R. Yoshiyah) or the study house (R. Yonatan in R. Elazar's name). The participle stands twice in the Torah, both here — machine-checked.
middah: E10 (repetition signifies — 15:33's 'gathering' repeating 15:32's teaches the forewarning; R. Yitzchak's I1 a-fortiori from idolatry frees the repetition to teach that the warning names the labor; the inverted verse / the study house)

check.note: the participle 'gathering' — its whole Torah career is the case's own two verses

claim_en: THE GUARD AND THE MODE. 'They placed him in the guard' — all liable to karet (the shelf's Hebrew; its emendation: to death) are confined pending judgment. 'It had not been declared what should be done to him' — but Exod 31:14 already sentences the profaner to death; what was undeclared is WHICH DEATH: the uncertainty is the mode (Sanhedrin 78b:7's distinction from the blasphemer, at its source). Onkelos: 'bound him in the guardhouse' — the same idiom as Lev 24:12; 'not explained TO THEM'.
middah: plain (the Sifrei's 'it is already written... what then does this teach' — the second statement narrowed to what the first lacked, the mode; the custody rule stated as a general from the case; the translation's shared guardhouse idiom)

check.note: 'in the guard' — the halt's word, Lev 24:12's

claim_en: THE OUTPUT FOR THE GENERATIONS AND THE HOUR. 'Die shall die the man' — for the generations; 'stone him with stones' — for the hour: the rule and the instance split inside one sentence, the rule being the MODE (stoning) for a statute that predates the case (Exod 31:14). 'All the congregation' — in its presence, not literally: Deut 17:7's witnesses first. The frame is the bare 'and the LORD said', no 'saying' and no statute in the speech — against Lev 24:13 and Num 9:9 (computed).
middah: plain (the Sifrei's split of one sentence — the doubled infinitive for the generations, the stoning clause for the hour; 'all the congregation' read as presence by Deut 17:7 in I13's third-verse shape; the bare frame an ink fact computed from the four outputs)

check.note: the output opens 'and he SAID' — not 'and he spoke... saying' (Lev 24:13, Num 9:9)

claim_en: THE EXECUTION: STONES AND A STONE. 'They brought him outside the camp' — the liable are executed outside the court. 'With stones' here against 'with a stone' at Lev 24:23 — reconciled by the stoning house's protocol: two stories, the first witness's push, the second witness's stone on the heart, then all Israel with stones — Deut 17:7's witnesses first and all the people after. 'As the LORD commanded' — stone and HANG (Deut 21:22, R. Eliezer). R. Chidka: Moses knew the death, not its mode — liability rolled through the liable. 'And he died' written here, absent at 24:23.
middah: I13 (two verses — 'with stones' at 15:35-36, 'with a stone' at Lev 24:23 — reconciled by the third, Deut 17:7's witnesses-first: the stoning house's protocol; the hanging from Deut 21:22, R. Eliezer's arm; outside the court; R. Chidka's liability through the liable; the death clause an ink delta)

check.note: the plural 'with stones' — the singular 'a stone' stands at Lev 24:23

claim_en: THE FRINGES' MAKING. Women included — R. Shimon exempts: a positive command that time causes, the rule stated here in full; the veil exempt, the wrap obligated (R. Yehuda b. Bava). 'Fringe' = what protrudes, of any amount — no measure (the elders in Yonatan b. Beteira's upper room; nor the lulav). Not one thread: 'cords' (Deut 22:12) — three (Beth Hillel) / three white and the fourth blue (Beth Shammai, the law). The cord from the corner, the fringe from the cord. FOUR corners (Deut 22:12) exclude the rest; pillows excluded ('cover yourself'); night garments excluded ('you shall see it'); the blind included ('it shall be for you'). The blue spun and doubled, the white by the shared 'place'; at the weaving, not the growing (R. Eliezer b. Yaakov: both); tied, not woven. Onkelos: kruspedin, the Greek loanword; 'covering' for 'garment'.
middah: E2 (restriction — 'cords' and 'fringe' each limiting the other; the corners limited to four by Deut 22:12; pillows by 'cover yourself'; the night by 'you shall see it'; with E1 inclusion — women, the blind man's garment; and I2 — the white spun and doubled from the shared verb 'place'; R. Shimon's time-bound rule and the houses' count recorded)

claim_en: SEEING AND REMEMBERING. The four are one mitzvah, mutually inclusive — R. Yishmael: four. The names: blue from the Egyptians' bereavement or destruction, fringe from 'He peered' (Song 2:9). R. Meir: 'you shall see HIM' — as receiving the Shekhinah's face (blue, sea, firmament, Throne). 'See and remember' — see this command and remember another: the Shema, tied by 15:41's 'I am the LORD your God' found only in the Shema's sections; the three sections' order (the kingdom's yoke, the commands' yoke, the fringes by day); R. Shimon b. Yochai: learn, teach, do; the a-fortiori from the fringes to every command. 'After your hearts' heresy, 'your eyes' harlotry, 'go astray' idolatry; the eyes follow the heart. Onkelos: 'the thought of your heart and the sight of your eyes'.
middah: I2 (the shared 'I am the LORD your God' of 15:41 ties the fringes' 'remember' to the Shema's recitation; the sections' order from 'you shall see it'; with the recorded readings — one mitzvah or four (R. Yishmael), 'see Him' (R. Meir), the E5 a-fortiori from the sign to the deed, heart/eyes/astray as heresy/harlotry/idolatry; Onkelos's two supplied nouns)

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 115:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 115:2; Onkelos Num 15:40; Onkelos Num 15:41
claim_en: REMEMBER IS DO; THE TWO 'I AM'. 'So that you remember and do' equates remembering with doing; 'holy to your God' — all the commands' holiness, or the fringes' own (Rebbi: they add holiness). 'Who brought you out of Egypt' — against imitation dye for blue: the secret sinner exposed as Egypt was; the servant parable — redeemed as servants, the light and heavy decrees (the Sabbath, illicit unions, the fringes, the tefillin) on that condition. 'I am the LORD your God' AGAIN after Exod 20:2 — against 'we will not do and not receive' (Ezekiel 20's elders; pestilence, sword, famine, then rule perforce). R. Natan: the reward at the command's side — the four fringes as four witnesses, the doubled 'I am' reward and punishment.
middah: E10 (repetition signifies — 'I am the LORD your God' twice at 15:41 after Exod 20:2: the second against 'we will not do'; R. Natan's reward and punishment, four witnesses) with E26 (the servant parable; the imitation-dye measure) — remembering equated with doing, the fringes' own holiness (Rebbi)
